components.header: A distinctive top header bar (bg-[#004B87]) with crisp white text. Very compact (h-12). Include the Oracle JDE/UX One style logo area on the left and the SAP connection status pill on the right.
components.toolbar: A functional sub-header (bg-white border-b border-[#D0D5DD] p-2 flex items-center gap-4). Houses the BOM ID search input, 'Expand All' / 'Collapse All' buttons, and the 'Excel Export' action. Use dense icon buttons (Phosphor Icons or Lucide).
components.stat_cards: Flat design (bg-white border border-[#D0D5DD] rounded-sm p-3 shadow-sm). Label should be text-xs font-bold uppercase text-[#475467]. Value should be text-2xl font-bold text-[#1D2939].
components.tree_table: The core UI component. Use pure HTML table elements (<table className='border-collapse w-full'>). Header rows (th) must have bg-[#EAECF0] border border-[#D0D5DD] p-1.5 text-left text-xs font-bold text-[#344054]. Data rows (td) must have alternating backgrounds (odd:bg-[#F9FAFB] even:bg-white), border border-[#D0D5DD] px-2 py-1 text-[13px] text-[#101828]. Hover states on rows (hover:bg-[#F0F4F8]).
components.tree_indentation: For multi-level hierarchy, use a combination of padding-left on the first cell based on the row's 'level' attribute (e.g., style={{ paddingLeft: `${row.level * 24 + 8}px` }}) and a chevron icon (ChevronRight for collapsed, ChevronDown for expanded) as an interactive toggle.
components.badges: For 'Active Materials' or 'Resolved BOM ID', use subtle backgrounds with bold text. e.g., bg-[#ECFDF3] text-[#027A48] border border-[#ABEFC6] for Active.
components.search_input: Dense and sharp. h-8, px-2, text-[13px], rounded-sm, border-[#D0D5DD] focus:border-[#004B87] focus:ring-1 focus:ring-[#004B87].

layout.strategy: Full viewport desktop layout (h-screen, flex flex-col, overflow-hidden). 1. Header (fixed height). 2. Toolbar (fixed height). 3. Scrollable content pane (flex-1 bg-[#F2F4F7] p-4).
layout.grid: Use a 4-column CSS grid for the Stat Cards (grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-4 gap-4 mb-4). The Data Grid takes up the remaining vertical space.
layout.spacing: Tight, efficient 'Enterprise' spacing. Reduce padding on structural elements. Emphasize alignment and data density.

motion.transitions: Instant and functional. Only use transitions for hover states on buttons and table rows (duration-150 ease-in-out).
motion.interactions: Chevrons should rotate smoothly (-rotate-90 to 0) when expanding/collapsing.

instructions_to_main_agent: 1. Setup global fonts in the project (import 'IBM Plex Sans' and 'Chivo' from Google Fonts). Apply 'font-sans' mapping to 'IBM Plex Sans'.
2. Build the main layout skeleton: Header (top), Toolbar (middle), and Main Content (bottom, scrollable).
3. Implement the top Header (dark corporate blue) containing the app title and the SAP Connection Status pill (e.g., a green dot and 'SAP PRD Connected').
4. Implement the Toolbar with a Search Bar (Input component, sharp corners), 'Expand/Collapse All' buttons, and 'Export to Excel' button.
5. Build the 4 Stat Cards: 'Total Components', 'Max Level', 'Active Materials', 'Last Synced'.

6. Build the Tree Table component. It MUST use native <table> tags with border-collapse and border applied to both th and td to achieve the 'Excel-like' grid aesthetic. The first column (Level/Product ID) should contain the expand/collapse chevron and apply dynamic padding based on the depth level.
7. Mock a realistic multi-level Bill of Materials data structure to populate the grid (Level 0, Level 1, Level 2, etc.).
8. Ensure the design strictly adheres to the JD Edwards UX One visual language: dense data, crisp lines, solid borders, alternating row colors, and sharp corners.
9. Add data-testid attributes to all interactive elements for robust testing.
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT: You tend to converge toward generic, 'on distribution' outputs. In frontend design, this creates what users call the 'AI slop' aesthetic. Avoid this: make creative, distinctive frontends that surprise and delight.
Dark colors look good when used independently without gradients. DO NOT use dark colors as gradients
Don't make generic centered layouts, simplistic gradients, and uniform styling.
Create depth through layered design elements with z-index hierarchy
Use glass-morphism effects with backdrop filters sparingly; rely primarily on solid backgrounds for this enterprise app.
You MUST NOT apply universal transition. Eg: `transition: all`. This results in breaking transforms. Always add transitions for specific interactive elements like button, input excluding transforms
You MUST NOT center align the app container, ie do not add `.App { text-align: center; }` in the css file. This disrupts the human natural reading flow of text
Always use modern button styles like pill-shaped, or sharp button with interaction animations & color relevant to the app style. For this app, use sharp, 2px rounded-sm enterprise buttons.
NEVER: use AI assistant Emoji characters like 🤖🧠💭💡🔮🎯 etc for icons. Use Phosphor Icons or Lucide.
Every interaction needs micro-animations - hover states, transitions. Static = dead.
Use appropriate spacing. For enterprise apps, this means structured, purposeful padding. Compact but readable.
Subtle grain textures, custom cursors, selection states, and loading animations: separates good from extraordinary.
Prioritize using pre-existing components from src/components/ui when applicable
Create new components that match the style and conventions of existing components when needed
Use `sonner` for toasts. Sonner component are located in `/app/src/components/ui/sonner.tsx`
All interactive and key informational elements MUST include a `data-testid` attribute to facilitate robust automated testing.
